redskin.summary: CONFIRMED: the user's belief is correct. Jolly Buoy and Red Skin operate on a strict 6-month rotation inside Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park (Wandoor): Jolly Buoy is open roughly 15 Nov - 14/15 May, and Red Skin is open the other half (16 May - 14 Nov per an operator's Feb-2026 page). So for 23-26 Sep 2026, Jolly Buoy is CLOSED and Red Skin is the island that is OPEN, and boats DO run from Wandoor Jetty in September (a 2026-season operator, MV WaveRider, sells Red Skin trips in this window), but every source stresses that departures are weather/sea-condition dependent during the SW monsoon and the Forest Department can cancel trips (partial refund of boat charges only). Permits: mandatory Forest Department entry permit, issued ONE DAY in advance (official tourism.andamannicobar.gov.in) from the Forest Dept at Wandoor or Port Blair/Sri Vijaya Puram with photo ID; operators/hotels can arrange it; ~150 visitors/day cap; day trips only, park entry sunrise-2 PM, Jolly Buoy noted closed on Mondays (trip dates Wed-Sat are unaffected). Logistics: Wandoor Jetty is ~25-30 km / 45-60 min by road from Port Blair; boat 25-45 min; morning departures only (reporting ~7-10:30 AM depending on boat, e.g. MV WaveRider reports 10:30 AM, departs 11 AM, back ~4 PM; older govt boats depart 8:30-10 AM, return 3-4 PM); time ashore ~2-4 hours. Allowed activities on Red Skin: swimming in shallow designated zones, supervised snorkeling, glass-bottom boat rides, beach time - all in approved areas. Costs (Indian nationals): permit Rs 50, boat Rs 300-500 (packaged trips from ~Rs 1,275-1,600 per person), snorkel set ~Rs 500, glass-bottom ride from ~Rs 1,000 per one source; strict plastic ban, no food stalls, carry photo ID.

activities.summary: All facts gathered in-browser. (A) DiveIndia (Havelock base: Beach No.5, White Sand Beach Resort, Govind Nagar; also a Neil branch at Bharatpur Beach 50m from jetty) runs a 2-day "Intro to Scuba" beginner program at Rs.14,000 pp all-inclusive (2 boat dives + confined-water day, possible shore dive) and states diving runs "all year round"; second operator Dive Andaman (Beach No.2, Govind Nagar) prices shore DSD Rs.5,500 +18% GST (~1 hr total, 30 min training + 35 min underwater), shore try-dive Rs.3,500, DSD by boat Rs.7,500. (B) Bioluminescence night kayaking on Havelock: Andaman Bliss charges Rs.3,500 pp (all taxes, 1-2 hr, sessions start ~3:30 AM, near Lighthouse/Beach No.5, age 13-45, basic swimming needed); Go2Andaman kayaking from Rs.2,800 and both operators say night/biolum kayaking happens only around no-moon/new-moon nights - and Sept 26, 2026 is a FULL MOON (Sept 25 = 98.5% waxing gibbous), so biolum kayaking during the Sept 23-27 trip is effectively ruled out. (C) Neil/Bharatpur: beach entry free, timings 5 AM-6 PM, jet ski Rs.800-1,200 for 10-15 min, guided snorkelling from Rs.3,500; scuba backup on Neil = DIVEIndia's Neil DIVEResort at Bharatpur Beach; May-Sept is off-season with weather-limited water sports. (D) Elephant Beach: no entry fee, speed-boat round trip Rs.1,000 pp rising to Rs.1,200 pp from September 2026, boats 9 AM-1 PM (~3-hr window, 20-min ride), 2-km/30-40-min jungle trek alternative; June-Sept monsoon means water sports often suspended and the beach may close some days with last-minute cancellations - open in principle but weather-dependent in late September. (E) Baratang: private-cab day tour Rs.8,400 (Go2Andaman, up to 2 pax - 3 adults likely costs more) or Rs.4,500 round-trip taxi + Rs.900 pp speedboat (Andaman Ocean); shared tours ~Rs.2,250-4,500 pp (Google snippets); hotel pickup 4:00-4:30 AM, Jirkatang convoy ~6:00 AM, caves ~9-10 AM, back in Port Blair ~3:30-4:00 PM, 10-12 hrs door-to-door, tour runs all days. (F) Chidiya Tapu: beach free (5 AM-6 PM, area clears by 7 PM), Biological Park Rs.25 (10 AM-5 PM, closed Mondays), Munda Pahad trek strictly 11 AM-3 PM with gate closing 3 PM sharp, 1.5 km/45-60 min, sunset 5:30-6 PM, cab from Port Blair Rs.1,500-3,500, trails slippery in monsoon. (G) Cellular Jail light-and-sound show: Rs.300 adult / Rs.150 child, ~45 min; Hindi 5:50/7:50/8:50 PM daily + 6:50 PM Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun, English 6:50 PM Mon/Wed/Fri, closed national holidays.
